subject: chem
title: Hydrocarbons
syllabus: Classification, isomerism, IUPAC nomenclature, general methods of preparation, properties and reactions. Alkanes — conformations: Sawhorse and Newman projections (of ethane); mechanism of halogenation of alkanes. Alkenes — geometrical isomerism; mechanism of electrophilic addition: addition of hydrogen, halogens, water, hydrogen halides (Markownikoff's and peroxide effect); ozonolysis and polymerization. Alkynes — acidic character; addition of hydrogen, halogens, water and hydrogen halides; polymerization. Aromatic hydrocarbons — nomenclature, benzene: structure and aromaticity; mechanism of electrophilic substitution: halogenation, nitration, Friedel-Crafts alkylation and acylation, directive influence of the functional group in mono-substituted benzene.

body: Preparation: hydrogenation of alkenes/alkynes (Pt, Pd, Ni); RX + Zn/H^{+}; Wurtz 2RX + 2Na → R–R (even C); decarboxylation RCOONa + NaOH/CaO → R–H (one C less); Kolbe electrolysis 2RCOONa → R–R.
Free-radical halogenation (Cl_{2}/hν): number of monochlorides = kinds of H. Conformations of ethane: staggered (60°, most stable) vs eclipsed (12.5 kJ/mol higher).
Branching lowers b.p. Isomerisation (AlCl_{3}/HCl), aromatisation (n-hexane → benzene, heptane → toluene), pyrolysis/cracking.
Prepared by dehydrohalogenation (alc. KOH, Saytzeff: more substituted alkene), dehydration of alcohols (conc. H_{2}SO_{4}), partial reduction of alkynes (Lindlar → cis; Na/liq. NH_{3} → trans).
Electrophilic addition. HX: Markovnikov (via the more stable carbocation). HBr + peroxide: anti-Markovnikov (radical); not with HCl or HI.
Ozonolysis (O_{3}, then Zn/H_{2}O): each C=C → two C=O. Baeyer test: cold dil. alkaline KMnO_{4} decolourises (glycol). Hot acidic KMnO_{4} cleaves to acids/ketones.

check.why: Br• adds to the CH₂ end.

body: Prepared from vicinal dihalides with alc. KOH then NaNH_{2}; ethyne from CaC_{2} + H_{2}O.
Terminal ≡C–H is acidic (sp C): reacts with Na, NaNH_{2}, ammoniacal AgNO_{3}/Cu_{2}Cl_{2} (but-2-yne does not).
Hydration (HgSO_{4}/H_{2}SO_{4}, 333 K): ethyne → ethanal, other alkynes → ketones. Red-hot iron tube: 3 HC≡CH → benzene; propyne → mesitylene.

Aromatic: planar, 6π, resonance-stabilised → substitution (keeps the ring) rather than addition. Electrophiles: NO_{2}^{+} (HNO_{3}/H_{2}SO_{4}), Br^{+} (Br_{2}/FeBr_{3}), SO_{3}, R^{+}/RCO^{+} (AlCl_{3}).
o/p directors & activators: –OH, –NH_{2}, –OR, –NHCOR, –R. Halogens: o/p but deactivating. m directors & deactivators: –NO_{2}, –CN, –CHO, –COR, –COOH, –SO_{3}H.

Friedel–Crafts fails on strongly deactivated rings (nitrobenzene) and on aniline (–NH_{2} binds AlCl_{3}). Alkylation rearranges (n-PrCl → cumene) and over-alkylates. Benzpyrene-type PAHs are carcinogenic.

formulas: C_{x}H_{y} needs x + y/4 mol O_{2}
traps: Kolbe electrolysis of CH₃COONa gives ETHANE, not methane.
Benzene does not decolourise bromine water.
n-Propyl chloride + benzene/AlCl₃ gives mostly cumene.

pyq.q: An optically active alkyl halide C_{4}H_{9}Br [A] reacts with hot KOH dissolved in ethanol and forms alkene [B] as major product which reacts with bromine to give dibromide [C]. The compound [C] is converted into a gas [D] upon reacting with alcoholic NaNH_{2}. During hydration 18 gram of water is added to 1 mole of gas [D] on warming with mercuric sulphate and dilute acid at 333 K to form compound [E]. The IUPAC name of compound [E] is :
sol: A must be chiral: 2-bromobutane. Saytzeff elimination → B but-2-ene → C 2,3-dibromobutane → double dehydrohalogenation → D but-2-yne (gas).
Hg^{2+}/H^{+} hydration of but-2-yne → enol → E butan-2-one.

pyq.q: Identify the correct set of reagents or reaction conditions 'X' and 'Y' in the following set of transformation. CH_{3}–CH_{2}–CH_{2}–Br → ('X') Product → ('Y') CH_{3}–CH(Br)–CH_{3}
sol: Hot alcoholic NaOH eliminates HBr → propene (aqueous NaOH would give propanol).
HBr adds to propene by Markovnikov's rule → 2-bromopropane. (Br_{2} would give a dibromide.)
o: X = dil.aq. NaOH, 20°C, Y = HBr/acetic acid
X = conc.alc. NaOH, 80°C, Y = HBr/acetic acid

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Ozonolysis followed by treatment with Zn, H_{2}O of cis-2-butene gives ethanal. Statement II: The product obtained by ozonolysis followed by treatment with Zn, H_{2}O of 3, 6-dimethyloct-4-ene has no chiral carbon atom. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: I: CH_{3}CH=CHCH_{3} splits into 2 CH_{3}CHO. True.
II: CH_{3}CH_{2}CH(CH_{3})CH=CHCH(CH_{3})CH_{2}CH_{3} gives 2 molecules of CH_{3}CH_{2}CH(CH_{3})CHO, whose C-2 is chiral. False.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are False
Statement I is false but Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

pyq.q: The reactions which cannot be applied to prepare an alkene by elimination, are: A. bromocyclohexane + NaOEt B. CH_{3}–CH_{2}–CH(Br)–CH_{3} + KOH (aq) C. (CH_{3})_{3}C–Br + NaOMe D. phenol + Na_{2}Cr_{2}O_{7}/H_{2}SO_{4} E. (CH_{3})_{3}C–OH + Cu, 573 K
sol: A, C: strong alkoxide bases with 2°/3° halides → E2 alkenes. E: a 3° alcohol is dehydrated (not dehydrogenated) over Cu at 573 K → 2-methylpropene.
B: aqueous KOH mainly substitutes → butan-2-ol. D: oxidation of phenol gives benzoquinone, not an alkene.

pyq.q: The number of optically active products obtained from the complete ozonolysis of the given compound is: CH_{3}–CH=CH–CH(CH_{3})–CH=CH–CH(CH_{3})–CH=CH–CH_{3} (the two CH(CH_{3}) carbons are stereocentres)
sol: Each C=C is cut: products 2 CH_{3}CHO and 2 OHC–CH(CH_{3})–CHO.
In methylpropanedial the CH carries two identical –CHO groups → not chiral. No optically active product: 0.

pyq.q: The incorrect statement regarding ethyne is
sol: C≡C (120 pm, 823 kJ/mol) is shorter and STRONGER than C=C (134 pm, 681 kJ/mol).
Ethyne carbons are sp; the molecule is linear.
o: The C-C bonds in ethyne is shorter than that in ethene
The carbon-carbon bonds in ethyne is weaker than that in ethene

pyq.q: One mole of an alkane (x) requires 8 mole oxygen for complete combustion. Sum of number of carbon and hydrogen atoms in the alkane (x) is _______ .

The compound (X) on (i) on heating in the presence of anhydrous AlCl_{3} and HCl gas gives 2,4-dimethyl pentane (ii) aromatization gives toulene and (iii) cyclisation gives methyl cyclohexane. The correct name of compound (X) is :
sol: AlCl_{3}/HCl isomerises an alkane into a branched isomer (C_{7}H_{16} → 2,4-dimethylpentane).
n-Heptane over Cr_{2}O_{3}/V_{2}O_{5} (773 K) cyclises to methylcyclohexane and aromatises to toluene. X = heptane.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : One mole of propyne reacts with excess of sodium to liberate half a mole of H_{2} gas. Statement II: Four g of propyne reacts with NaNH_{2} to liberate NH_{3} gas which occupies 224 mL at STP. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: I: propyne has one acidic ≡C–H: CH_{3}C≡CH + Na → CH_{3}C≡CNa + ½H_{2}. True.
II: 4 g = 0.1 mol → 0.1 mol NH_{3} = 2240 mL, not 224 mL. False.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

pyq.q: The alkane from below having two secondary hydrogens is :
sol: Secondary H are on CH_{2} groups bonded to two carbons.
2,2,3,3-Tetramethylpentane has a single CH_{2} (C-4) → 2 secondary H; the others have 4 or more.

pyq.q: The incorrect statement regarding conformations of ethane is:
sol: Staggered is the most stable (least torsional strain); eclipsed is the least stable, ~12.5 kJ/mol higher.
Rotation interconverts the infinitely many conformations.
o: Ethane has infinite number of conformations
The dihedral angle in staggered conformation is 60°
Eclipsed conformation is the most stable conformation.
The conformations of ethane are interconvertible to one-another.

pyq.q: "P" is a hydrocarbon of molecular formula C_{8}H_{14}. On ozonolysis, "P" forms "Q". "Q" on treatment with alkali under reflux condition produces "R", which on treatment with I_{2}/NaOH gives a yellow precipitate. Acidification of the solution gives "S" = 2-methylcyclopent-1-ene-1-carboxylic acid. The correct structure of "P" is
sol: Work back: S comes from R = 1-acetyl-2-methylcyclopentene by the haloform reaction (CH_{3}CO– → –COOH).
R is the intramolecular aldol product of Q = octane-2,7-dione, which is the ozonolysis product of 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene (C_{8}H_{14}).

pyq.q: But-2-yne and hydrogen (one mole each) are separately treated with (i) Pd/C and (ii) Na/liq.NH_{3} to give the products X and Y respectively. Identify the incorrect statements. A. X and Y are stereoisomers. B. Dipole moment of X is zero. C. Boiling point of X is higher than Y. D. X and Y react with O_{3}/Zn + H_{2}O to give different products.
sol: Pd/C (syn) → X cis-but-2-ene; Na/liq. NH_{3} → Y trans-but-2-ene. They are stereoisomers.
cis has a dipole (B wrong) and a higher b.p. than trans (C right). Both give 2 CH_{3}CHO on ozonolysis (D wrong).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Methane can be prepared by decarboxylation of sodium ethanoate, Kolbe's electrolysis of sodium acetate and reaction of CH_{3}MgBr with water. Statement II: Methane cannot be prepared from unsaturated hydrocarbons and by Wurtz reaction. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: I: decarboxylation (CH_{3}COONa + NaOH/CaO) and CH_{3}MgBr + H_{2}O give CH_{4}, but Kolbe electrolysis of CH_{3}COONa gives ethane. False.
II: hydrogenating an alkene/alkyne or Wurtz coupling always gives ≥ 2 carbons. True.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: An alkane (Y) requires 8 moles of oxygen for complete combustion and on chlorination with Cl_{2}/hν, (Y) gives only one monochlorinated product (Z). The total number of primary carbon atoms in (Y) is ______.
sol: Only one kind of H → neopentane C(CH_{3})_{4}: 4 primary carbons.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements for the reaction sequence: Compound 'X' (C_{3}H_{6}Cl_{2}) → excess NaNH_{2} → Compound 'Y'; Y → dil. H_{2}SO_{4}, Hg^{2+} → Compound 'Z'; Y → red hot iron tube, Δ → Compound 'Q' (C_{9}H_{12}). Statement I: Compound 'Z' will give yellow precipitate with NaOI. Statement II: Compound 'Q' has two different types of 'H' atoms (aromatic : aliphatic) in the ratio 1 : 3. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: X (a dichloropropane) → Y propyne. Hydration → Z acetone (CH_{3}CO– → iodoform with NaOI). True.
Cyclic trimerisation → Q mesitylene, 1,3,5-(CH_{3})_{3}C_{6}H_{3}: 3 ring H : 9 methyl H = 1 : 3. True.
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

pyq.q: Ph–CH=CH_{2} + HBr in presence of (PhCOO)_{2} → Product. A. The reaction proceeds through a more stable radical intermediate. B. The role of peroxide is to generate H^{•} (Hydrogen radical). C. During this reaction, benzene is formed as a byproduct. D. 1-Bromo-2-phenylethane is formed as the minor product. E. The same reaction in absence of peroxide proceeds via carbocation intermediate. Identify the correct statements.
sol: Br^{•} adds to CH_{2} giving the benzylic radical (A ✓) → PhCH_{2}CH_{2}Br is the MAJOR product (D ✗). Without peroxide: ionic, via PhCH^{+}CH_{3} (E ✓).

pyq.q: 3-Methylhex-2-ene on reaction with HBr in presence of peroxide forms an addition product (A). The number of possible stereoisomers for 'A' is
sol: Peroxide effect: Br^{•} adds to C-2 to leave the tertiary radical at C-3 → A = 2-bromo-3-methylhexane.
C-2 and C-3 are both chiral and different → 2^{2} = 4.

pyq.q: An optically active alkyl bromide C_{4}H_{9}Br, reacts with ethanolic KOH to form major compound [A] which reacts with bromine to give compound [B]. Compound [B] reacts with ethanolic KOH and sodamide to give compound [C]. One molecule of water adds to compound [C] on warming with mercuric sulphate and dilute sulphuric acid at 333 K to form compound [D]. The functional group in compound D will be confirmed by :
sol: 2-Bromobutane → but-2-ene → 2,3-dibromobutane → but-2-yne → butan-2-one (D).
A methyl ketone (CH_{3}CO–) gives the haloform (iodoform) test.

pyq.q: X g of nitrobenzene on nitration gave 4.2 g of m -dinitrobenzene. X = _____ g. (nearest integer) [Given : molar mass (in g mol^{−1}) C : 12, H : 1, O : 16, N : 14 ]

Given below are two statements : Statement I: Nitration of benzene involves the following step: H–O^{+}(H)–NO_{2} ⇌ H_{2}O + NO_{2}^{+}. Statement II: Use of Lewis base promotes the electrophilic substitution of benzene. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: I: protonated nitric acid loses water to give the nitronium ion. Correct.
II: a Lewis ACID (FeBr_{3}, AlCl_{3}) generates the electrophile; a Lewis base would not. Incorrect.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

pyq.q: Number of compounds from the following which cannot undergo Friedel-Crafts reactions is : toluene, nitrobenzene, xylene, cumene, aniline, chlorobenzene, m-nitroaniline, m-dinitrobenzene
sol: Strongly deactivated rings (–NO_{2}) fail, and –NH_{2} binds AlCl_{3} (becomes –NH_{2}^{+}AlCl_{3}^{−}).
Cannot: nitrobenzene, aniline, m-nitroaniline, m-dinitrobenzene = 4. (Chlorobenzene reacts, slowly.)

pyq.q: Identify the correct statements : The presence of –NO_{2} group in benzene ring A. activates the ring towards electrophilic substitutions. B. deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitutions. C. activates the ring towards nucleophilic substitutions. D. deactivates the ring towards nucleophilic substitutions.
sol: –NO_{2} withdraws electrons (−R, −I): the ring is poorer in electrons → slower attack by E^{+} …
… and better at stabilising the anionic σ-complex of nucleophilic attack (o/p-nitro aryl halides react readily).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : On nitration of m-xylene with HNO_{3}, H_{2}SO_{4} followed by oxidation, 4-nitrobenzene-1,3-dicarboxylic acid is obtained as the major product. Statement (II): –CH_{3} group is o/p-directing while –NO_{2} group is m-directing group. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: In m-xylene, C-4 is ortho to one CH_{3} and para to the other (and less hindered than C-2) → 4-nitro-m-xylene; KMnO_{4} oxidises both CH_{3} → 4-nitrobenzene-1,3-dicarboxylic acid. True.
II is the standard directing rule. True.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Benzene is nitrated to give nitrobenzene, which on further treatment with CH_{3}COCl/AlCl_{3} will give m-nitroacetophenone. Statement II: –NO_{2} group is a m-directing, and deactivating group. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
sol: Nitrobenzene is too deactivated for Friedel–Crafts acylation (it is even used as an FC solvent) → no m-nitroacetophenone. I incorrect.
II is correct.
o: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

pyq.q: For the following Friedel Craft's alkylation reaction, which of the statements are correct? Benzene + CH_{3}CH_{2}CH_{2}Cl (anhydrous AlCl_{3}) → Alkylbenzene. A. Major product is n-propyl benzene. B. iso-propyl carbocation intermediate is also generated. C. Multiple substitution is inevitable. D. Introducing electron-donating substituent on benzene will not produce any alkyl benzene.
sol: The 1° carbocation rearranges (hydride shift) to the 2° isopropyl cation → cumene is major (A ✗, B ✓).
The alkyl product is more reactive than benzene, so polyalkylation always occurs (C ✓). Donor groups speed up FC alkylation (D ✗).

pyq.q: Consider: 4-Nitrotoluene → (i) Sn, HCl/Δ (ii) pH neutralisation → (A) → (i) (CH_{3}CO)_{2}O (ii) Br_{2}/AcOH → (B). Assuming that the reaction proceeds to completion, then 137 mg of 4 -nitrotoluene will produce _____ mg of B. (Given molar mass in g mol^{−1} H : 1, C : 12, N : 14, O : 16, Br : 80 )
sol: A = p-toluidine → acetylation → 4-methylacetanilide; –NHCOCH_{3} directs Br ortho to itself → B = 2-bromo-4-methylacetanilide, C_{9}H_{10}BrNO (228).
137 mg = 1 mmol → 228 mg.

pyq.q: Consider the following reaction of benzene: C_{6}H_{6} + CH_{3}–CO–CH_{2}–CH_{2}–COCl (anhydrous AlCl_{3}) → (P) → aq NaOH, Δ → (Q). In compound (Q), the percentage of oxygen is _______%. (Nearest integer)
sol: FC acylation at the acid chloride: P = C_{6}H_{5}CO–CH_{2}CH_{2}–COCH_{3}, a 1,4-diketone.
Intramolecular aldol condensation (CH_{3} enolate onto the PhC=O) → Q = 3-phenylcyclopent-2-en-1-one, C_{11}H_{10}O (158): % O = 16/158 = 10.1 ≈ 10.
